title: Hands-on Exercise 1: Geospatial Data Wrangling with R
text: This exercise works through the core geospatial data science workflow in R: importing geospatial and aspatial data, checking and setting coordinate reference systems, converting aspatial data to spatial data, and performing basic geoprocessing with the sf package.

Note on format: the original exercise reference uses the Master Plan boundary and pre-school location layers in Shapefile/KML format. Both have since been retired on the data.gov.sg portal in favour of GeoJSON-only downloads, so this write-up imports the GeoJSON versions directly with st_read() instead. The underlying sf workflow is identical regardless of source format.
The Cycling Path dataset from LTA DataMall (used in the reference chapter’s buffer geoprocessing example) requires a DataMall API account to download, which I did not have set up in time for this submission. That section is noted but not run below; I’ll revisit it once I have API access.

Both layers come in as WGS84 (EPSG:4326 / CRS84), Singapore’s projected coordinate system is SVY21 (EPSG:3414), which is needed for any accurate area or distance calculation. Transforming both layers:

mpsz3414 <- st_transform(mpsz, crs = 3414)
preschool3414 <- st_transform(preschool, crs = 3414)

section: 8. Importing and Converting an Aspatial Data Set
text:
8. Importing and Converting an Aspatial Data Set
The Airbnb listings CSV has latitude/longitude columns but no spatial geometry — it needs to be converted into an sf object before it can be used alongside the other two layers.

listings <- read_csv("data/aspatial/listings.csv")


listings_sf <- st_as_sf(listings,
                         coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                         crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)

text:
9. Geoprocessing with sf Package

9.1 Point-in-polygon count: pre-schools per subzone

mpsz3414$`PreSch Count` <- lengths(st_intersects(mpsz3414, preschool3414))


summary(mpsz3414$`PreSch Count`)

   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
   0.00    0.00    4.00    7.09   10.00   72.00 




9.2 Subzone area and pre-school density

mpsz3414$Area <- mpsz3414 %>%
  st_area()

mpsz3414 <- mpsz3414 %>%
  mutate(`PreSch Density` = as.numeric(`PreSch Count`) / (as.numeric(Area) / 1000000))


ggplot(data = mpsz3414, aes(x = `PreSch Density`)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "black", fill = "light blue") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of pre-school density by subzone",
       x = "Pre-school density (per sq km)",
       y = "Number of subzones")









ggplot(data = mpsz3414, aes(y = `PreSch Count`, x = `PreSch Density`)) +
  geom_point(color = "black", fill = "light blue") +
  labs(title = "Pre-school count vs. density by subzone",
       x = "Pre-school density (per sq km)",
       y = "Pre-school count")

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: Geospatial Data Wrangling with R
text:
10. Reflections
The main friction point in this exercise wasn’t the sf workflow itself, it was that the reference chapter’s data sources have moved on: data.gov.sg no longer serves the Master Plan boundary or pre-school layers as Shapefile/KML, only GeoJSON, and the LTA DataMall cycling path layer sits behind an API key I hadn’t set up yet. st_read() handles GeoJSON exactly the same way it handles a Shapefile or KML, so the substitution didn’t change anything downstream — the point-in-polygon and density workflow ran the same way once both layers were reprojected to EPSG:3414.
